title: Exceptions, custom exceptions, defensive programming, and logging
objectives: Use throw, try, catch, and finally with the official rule that at least catch or finally must accompany try.
Create a custom exception class that extends Exception and ends with Exception.
Name exceptions that cannot be caught, including LimitException, and explain that finally is skipped too.
Use debug logs and System.debug as diagnostics, not as a substitute for catching governors or swallowing Exception.
diagnostic_question: A service catches Exception around DML and SOQL, logs nothing, and returns null. A bulk load then hits a governor. What still rolls back, what cannot be caught, and how would you redesign the catch and logging?
definition: Apex uses exceptions to signal errors that disrupt normal flow. throw raises them; try/catch/finally recover when the exception is catchable. Custom exception classes extend Exception and must be named *Exception. Some platform exceptions—including LimitException—cannot be caught, and finally does not run for those. Debug logs record the transaction. ([Exception Statements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_statements.htm); [Exceptions in Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_definition.htm))
why_it_matters: Swallowing Exception hides DmlException, QueryException, and still cannot save you from governors. Interviewers want custom types for caller contracts, finally for cleanup that is not a second transaction, and debug logs instead of System.debug in production loops.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a building fire panel. throw pulls an alarm. catch is the floor warden for a labeled alarm type. finally is the checklist that still runs after a normal alarm—unlock the stairwell, close the log. A custom exception is a labeled pull-station you install for your service. LimitException is a full-building evacuation: the local panel is skipped, including finally. The debug log is the alarm printout. Do not tape over the master alarm and return null.
deeper_explanation: try identifies code that may throw. catch handles a unique type; Exception must be last. finally always runs for catchable exceptions. At least one catch or finally is required with try. ([Exception Statements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_statements.htm))

LimitException (governor), assertion failures, and license exceptions cannot be caught; catch and finally do not execute. Unhandled exceptions roll back processed DML, write debug logs, email LastModifiedBy by default, and show a UI error. ([Exception Statements](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_statements.htm); [Exceptions in Apex](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_definition.htm))

Custom exceptions extend Exception, must end with Exception, inherit getMessage/getCause/getLineNumber/getStackTraceString, and can wrap an inner exception. ([Create Custom Exceptions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_exception_custom.htm))

Defensive programming here means catch specific types, rethrow or wrap with context, and log with trace flags—not catch (Exception e) { return null; }. Debug logs record database operations and errors; class/trigger trace flags override levels but do not by themselves start logging. ([Debug Log](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_debugging_debug_log.htm))

mental_model.analogy: A building fire panel: labeled pull-stations, floor wardens, and a full-building evacuation that skips the local panel.
useful_mapping: catch (DmlException) → floor warden for that alarm type
catch (Exception) last → the lobby desk that only speaks after specialists
finally → stairwell checklist after a normal alarm
custom *Exception → a labeled pull-station your service installs
LimitException → building evacuation; local catch/finally skipped
where_it_breaks: finally is not a new transaction and cannot DML its way out of a LimitException.
Unhandled-exception email is not a monitoring product.
System.debug is not a durable audit log.
The analogy does not encode governor numbers (APEX-007).

claims.claim: try requires at least one catch or finally. catch types must be unique; Exception must be last. LimitException and assertion failures cannot be caught, and finally does not run for them.
claims.validation: Exception Statements in the Apex Developer Guide.

claims.claim: When an exception occurs, execution halts, processed DML is rolled back, and the event is logged. Unhandled exceptions email the LastModifiedBy developer by default and show a UI error.
Custom exception classes extend Exception and must have names ending in Exception. They can wrap an inner exception as the cause.
Debug logs record database operations, system processes, and errors. Class and trigger trace flags override levels but do not by themselves cause logs to be generated.

changed_in_release: API 41.0+ treats some unreachable statements after an unconditional throw as compile errors. Reverify the class API version.
unresolved_uncertainty: Exact debug-log retention counts and file-size caps should be read from current Monitoring documentation before quoting numbers.

telugu_glossary.telugu: Governor failure that cannot be caught.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Catch specific types, put Exception last, use finally for catchable cleanup. Custom types end with Exception. LimitException cannot be caught and skips finally. Unhandled errors roll back DML and write a debug log.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I never catch Exception to return null. I catch DmlException or QueryException, wrap in LAB_ShipmentException when the caller needs a domain contract, and rethrow otherwise. I set a user trace flag when I need a log; class flags only override levels. I tell interviewers governors are redesigned, not caught. Logging is not a second database of customer PII.

terminology.plain: An error object that stops normal Apex flow.
terminology.precise: A thrown instance (built-in or custom) that unwinds the stack until a matching catch or until the transaction fails.
terminology.example: throw new DmlException(); is unusual; insert of a bad row throws DmlException for you.
terminology.non_example: A validation-rule message with no Apex on the stack.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: addError on a trigger record: marks a row, not a thrown type unless it becomes DmlException.
terminology.boundary: Some platform exceptions cannot be caught.

terminology.plain: Your own exception type for a service contract.
terminology.precise: A class that extends Exception and whose name ends with Exception. Can wrap a cause.
terminology.non_example: public class LAB_ShipmentError (invalid name / not extending Exception).
terminology.confusable_neighbor: AuraHandledException for LWC/Aura (neighbor, not this lesson's focus).
terminology.boundary: Naming is required; an empty body still inherits constructors.

terminology.plain: The governor-limit failure you cannot catch.
terminology.precise: System.LimitException and similar critical exceptions abort execution; catch and finally do not run.
terminology.example: Too many SOQL queries in one transaction.
terminology.non_example: DmlException for a missing required field—that is catchable.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Catchable QueryException for a bad query.
terminology.boundary: Redesign/bulkify (APEX-007); do not wrap in try.

terminology.plain: A block that runs after try/catch for catchable paths.
terminology.precise: At most one finally per try. Runs whether or not a catchable exception occurred. Does not run for uncatchable exceptions.
terminology.example: finally { cr.Status__c = 'Closed'; } only if the exception was catchable and you still have a transaction.
terminology.boundary: finally is not a new governor pool.

terminology.plain: Failing in a controlled, specific way instead of hiding errors.
terminology.precise: Catch the narrowest type, preserve cause, do not return null from a swallowed Exception, and do not use try to 'handle' governors.
terminology.example: catch (DmlException e) { throw new LAB_ShipmentException('Stop insert failed', e); }
terminology.confusable_neighbor: allOrNone false (APEX-005): that is DML policy, not exception policy.
terminology.boundary: Defense is not the same as catching everything.

terminology.plain: The platform trace of a transaction.
terminology.precise: A log that can include database operations, system processes, and errors. User trace flags start capture; class/trigger flags override levels only.
terminology.example: Setup → Debug Logs → user trace flag, then reproduce the LAB_ failure.
terminology.non_example: System.debug in a 200-row loop as the only production observability.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Unhandled exception email: a notification, not the full log.
terminology.boundary: Retention/size are org-sensitive; do not invent caps.

when_to_use: When an Apex class must throw or catch DmlException/QueryException instead of returning null.
When a custom exception is the right contract for callers of a service method.
When defensive programming means narrow catch blocks plus debug-log evidence.
When explaining logging via debug logs and why LimitException cannot be handled.
when_not_to_use: Do not use try/catch as a substitute for bulkification when a governor LimitException is the real defect (APEX-007).
Do not catch Exception in a trigger to hide addError or DML failures.
Do not treat System.debug as durable logging or as a place for customer secrets.
Do not use this exceptions lesson as a DML allOrNone guide (APEX-005) or a trigger-order map (APEX-009).

decision_table.signal: DML failed on a required field and the caller should see a domain error.
decision_table.choose: catch (DmlException) and throw a custom *Exception with the cause.
decision_table.why: Custom exceptions wrap inner exceptions; swallowing Exception hides the failure.

decision_table.signal: A test or load hits too many SOQL queries.
decision_table.choose: Redesign/bulkify; do not write a catch for LimitException.
decision_table.not: try/catch/finally around the loop hoping to recover.
decision_table.why: LimitException cannot be caught; finally does not run.

decision_table.signal: You need a log of a failing sandbox transaction.
decision_table.choose: User debug-log trace flag, optionally with class-level overrides.
decision_table.not: Only a class trace flag with no logging enabled.
decision_table.why: Class/trigger flags override levels but do not start capture by themselves.

decision_table.signal: Cleanup must run after both success and catchable failure.
decision_table.choose: finally on that try, knowing governors skip it.
decision_table.not: A second DML in finally as a way to undo LimitException.
decision_table.why: finally is for catchable paths; uncatchable aborts skip it.

limitations: Does not catalog every built-in exception type.
Debug-log retention numbers are not invented here.
AuraHandledException / LWC error shape is a neighbor.
security_notes: Do not System.debug secrets, session IDs, or real customer payloads.
Unhandled exception emails include org and user Ids—treat them as sensitive.
common_mistakes: Class trace flag without a user log.
Assuming finally runs after a governor abort.

troubleshooting.symptom: Compile error that a custom type is not an Exception.
No debug log file after a failure.
check: A user (or equivalent) trace flag that actually starts logging.
You reproduced after the flag was active.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: A class-only CLASS_TRACING flag is enough.

troubleshooting.symptom: catch and finally never ran on a bulk failure.
check: The failure is LimitException or another uncatchable type.
Redesign the SOQL/DML, do not add more catch blocks.

production_notes: Prefer specific catches and custom types at service boundaries.
Turn off leftover user trace flags.
No production deployment is authorized by this lesson.

options.B: DmlException from a missing required field

distractor_explanations.C: Custom exceptions you throw are catchable.

options.D: Only if you catch Exception first

distractor_explanations.B: That is true only for catchable paths.

mcqs.prompt: A custom exception class must do what?

options.A: Extend Exception and have a name ending in Exception

mcqs.prompt: What happens to processed DML when an exception occurs?

options.A: It is rolled back and not committed
options.B: It always commits row by row

distractor_explanations.B: That contradicts the rollback rule (partial success is APEX-005).

mcqs.prompt: Who receives unhandled Apex exception email by default?

options.A: The user in LastModifiedBy on the failing class or trigger

distractor_explanations.B: You can add more addresses; that is not the default.

options.A: Override log levels but do not start logging

distractor_explanations.B: You still need logging to be enabled (user flag, etc.).

mcqs.prompt: Which is defensive programming in this lesson?

options.A: catch (DmlException e) and wrap or rethrow with context
options.D: Delete the debug log so nobody sees the error

mcqs.rationale: Narrow catch plus preserved cause is the documented custom-exception pattern.

mcqs.prompt: getCause on a custom exception returns what?

options.A: The inner exception you passed to the constructor

mcqs.rationale: The custom-exception example passes the original DmlException as cause.

mcqs.prompt: Which statement separates an exception-handling class from business data?

interview_questions.question: How do try, catch, and finally work in Apex?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: try marks risky code. catch handles a unique type; Exception last. finally runs on catchable paths. You need at least catch or finally.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I catch DmlException or QueryException, not Exception first. I use finally for cleanup that is still in the same transaction. I state that LimitException skips both catch and finally so they hear I read Exception Statements. I do not treat finally as a new governor pool.
interview_questions.example: try { insert stops; } catch (DmlException e) { throw new LAB_ShipmentException('failed', e); } finally { System.debug('attempted'); }
tradeoffs: finally cleanup vs rollback in catch
follow_ups: Can you have try/finally with no catch?
What changed in API 41 for unreachable throw?
weak_answer_warnings: Saying finally always runs, including after governors

interview_questions.question: How do you create and use a custom exception?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Extend Exception, name it *Exception, throw it, and optionally pass the cause. Callers catch the domain type and can call getCause.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I show the guide's MerchandiseException pattern: catch DmlException, throw new MyException(message, e). That preserves the stack of the wrap line and the cause of the DML. I do not invent a second error-code enum unless the team already has one.
weak_answer_warnings: A class named LAB_ShipmentError that does not extend Exception

interview_questions.question: A teammate catches Exception around a trigger handler and returns. The load still dies with a governor. What do you teach?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: LimitException cannot be caught. Their catch never ran. They must bulkify, not wrap the loop.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I separate catchable DmlException from uncatchable LimitException. I ask for the debug log LIMIT_USAGE_FOR_NS. I refuse catch (Exception e) even for the DML path because it hides real row errors. I point them to APEX-007 for the redesign.
interview_questions.example: SOQL inside for (Account a : Trigger.new) still aborts the transaction.
follow_ups: What does Limits.getQueries show before abort?

interview_questions.question: You have no debug log after a failure, but a class trace flag exists. What is wrong?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Class flags override levels; they do not start logging. Add a user trace flag (or other start condition) and reproduce.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open Setup → Debug Logs, add myself, reproduce the LAB_ path, then download. I may raise the class to FINEST once capture is on. I do not System.debug secrets. I mention unhandled-exception email as a backup signal, not the full log.
interview_questions.example: CLASS_TRACING on LAB_ShipmentService with no user flag → zero files.
follow_ups: Do time-based workflows appear? (Guide says they do not.)
weak_answer_warnings: Blaming Salesforce for 'broken logs' without a user flag

interview_questions.question: When is catch (Exception e) acceptable?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Almost never at a service boundary. If used, it must be last, log, and rethrow or convert to a custom type—not return null.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I prefer specific types. A top-level Queueable might catch Exception to write a status row—but that DML can also fail, and it still cannot catch governors. I would rather fail loud in a trigger than swallow. Interviewers treat return-null catches as a fail.
interview_questions.example: catch (Exception e) { throw new LAB_ShipmentException('unexpected', e); } as last block.
follow_ups: How do you test the wrap?
Where do you store the status row without mixed DML?

interview_questions.question: What happens on an unhandled exception?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Execution stops, DML rolls back, a debug log can record it, LastModifiedBy gets email by default, and the UI shows an error.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I cite Exceptions in Apex. I mention you can add Apex Exception Email recipients. I mention Event Monitoring unexpected-exception files as optional, not as something I invent details for. I distinguish this from allOrNone false, where no exception is thrown for failed rows.
interview_questions.example: A trigger throws; the Account edit page shows an error and the insert did not commit.
tradeoffs: Email vs log vs Event Monitoring
follow_ups: What PII is in the email?
Does the running user get the email?

interview_questions.question: getCause() is null on your custom exception. Why?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You constructed it with only a message, not the original exception. Pass e into the constructor.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The guide shows throw new MerchandiseException('...', e). Without the cause, callers only see your wrap line. I also check they did not catch Exception and new up a blank exception. I print getStackTraceString to see the throw line.
tradeoffs: Wrap vs rethrow the same instance

interview_questions.question: How do exceptions interact with Database.insert(list, false)?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Partial success often throws nothing. Failures live on SaveResult. A later uncaught exception can still roll back the successes.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: This is the APEX-005 boundary. I inspect SaveResult instead of catching DmlException for that call. If I then throw a custom exception, I undo those partial inserts unless I wanted them kept—then I must not throw. Interviewers like people who can hold both models.
interview_questions.example: Database.insert(stops, false) then throw new LAB_ShipmentException if any !isSuccess—rolls back the good stops too.
tradeoffs: Keep partial rows vs fail the unit
follow_ups: Should a trigger use partial success?
weak_answer_warnings: Catching DmlException on allOrNone false as the only check
